                    ### Question
                    A 4-year-old girl is brought to the physician for a well-child examination. She has been healthy apart from an episode of bronchiolitis as an infant. Her 6-year-old sister recently underwent surgery for ventricular septal defect closure. She is at the 60th percentile for height and weight. Her mother is concerned about the possibility of the patient having a cardiovascular anomaly. Which of the following is most likely to indicate a benign heart murmur in this child?

                    ### Options
                    opa. A grade 3/6 systolic ejection murmur heard along the left lower sternal border that increases on valsalva
opb. A grade 4/6 midsystolic murmur at the right upper sternal border that increases on rapid squatting
opc. A grade 2/6 continuous murmur heard at the right supraclavicular region
opd. A grade 4/6 holosytolic murmur heard along the left lower sternal border that increases on hand grip
ope. A grade 3/6 holosytolic murmur at the apex that increases on hand grip

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
Innocent heart murmurs in children are typically systolic and grade 1-2/6. A grade 3/6 systolic ejection murmur heard along the left lower sternal border that increases on valsalva is more likely benign than a grade 2/6 continuous murmur at the right supraclavicular region. The presence of a continuous murmur is not indicative of a benign heart murmur in this case.
